title: Prime members
context: The growth team is preparing a Prime-exclusive promotion and needs the audience.
task: List the first_name, last_name and country of every customer who is a Prime member.
hint: Prime status is stored as a flag on the customers table — filter to the members.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name, country FROM customers WHERE prime_member = 1;

title: Catalogue for a price review
context: Merchandising is reviewing prices and wants the catalogue from cheapest to dearest.
task: Return name, category and price for every product, ordered from cheapest to most expensive.
hint: No filter needed — just sort the rows by the price column.
answer: SELECT name, category, price FROM products ORDER BY price, name;

title: Countries we ship to
context: Legal needs the list of countries where we have at least one customer.
task: Return each country that appears in the customers table, with no duplicates.
hint: A country appears on many customers — you want each one listed only once.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers;

title: Category menu
context: The storefront navigation lists every category once, alphabetically.
task: Return the distinct product categories, sorted A to Z.
hint: Take the unique values, then order them.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products ORDER BY category;

title: Well-stocked products
context: Merchandising wants to feature items we hold plenty of.
task: Return name and price for products with more than 50 units in stock, dearest first.
hint: Filter on the stock level, then sort by price high-to-low.
answer: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE stock > 50 ORDER BY price DESC;

title: Out of stock
context: Ops needs the list of products that cannot be sold right now.
task: Return product_id and name for every product that has no stock left.
hint: Out of stock means the stock level is exactly zero.
answer: SELECT product_id, name FROM products WHERE stock = 0;

title: High-value orders
context: Fraud review triages the most expensive orders first.
task: Return order_id, customer_id and total_amount for orders worth more than 300.
hint: Filter on the order's total value.
answer: SELECT order_id, customer_id, total_amount FROM orders WHERE total_amount > 300;

title: Cancellations to follow up
context: Support wants to reach out about cancelled orders.
task: Return order_id and order_date for every cancelled order.
hint: Match the status column to the right text value (text goes in single quotes).
answer: SELECT order_id, order_date FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled';

title: India Prime Day list
context: A regional Prime Day campaign is launching in India.
task: Return the first_name and last_name of customers who are in India and are Prime members.
hint: Two conditions both have to hold.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM customers WHERE country = 'India' AND prime_member = 1;

title: Home-tech landing page
context: A landing page features two categories together.
task: Return name and category for products in the Electronics or Kitchen categories.
hint: The category has to be one of a small set of values.
answer: SELECT name, category FROM products WHERE category IN ('Electronics','Kitchen');

title: Everything not delivered
context: Ops wants every order that is still open or went wrong.
task: Return order_id and status for orders whose status is anything other than delivered.
hint: You want the rows that do not match one value.
answer: SELECT order_id, status FROM orders WHERE status <> 'delivered';

title: Gifts under 100
context: A 'gifts' page shows mid-priced items.
task: Return name and price for products priced from 25 to 100 inclusive.
hint: An inclusive range on price.
answer: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 25 AND 100;

title: Q1 2024 orders
context: Finance is closing the first quarter of 2024.
task: Return order_id and order_date for orders placed during Q1 2024 (January through March).
hint: Dates are ISO text, so an inclusive range on order_date works — figure out the two endpoints.
answer: SELECT order_id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-03-31';

title: Kindle and Fire devices
context: The devices team tracks its own product lines.
task: Return name for products whose name begins with 'Kindle' or with 'Fire'.
hint: Pattern-match the start of the name.
answer: SELECT name FROM products WHERE name LIKE 'Kindle%' OR name LIKE 'Fire%';

title: Half-remembered name
context: Support is searching for a customer whose name contained 'an'.
task: Return first_name and last_name for customers whose first_name contains the letters 'an'.
hint: The pattern can appear anywhere in the text.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM customers WHERE first_name LIKE '%an%';

title: Uncontactable customers
context: A data-quality audit is finding customers we can't email.
task: Return customer_id, first_name and last_name for customers who have no email on file.
hint: A missing value is not the same as an empty string — test for the absence of a value.
answer: SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name FROM customers WHERE email IS NULL;

title: Corporate (non-warehouse) staff
context: HR needs the employees who aren't attached to any warehouse.
task: Return first_name, last_name and department for employees who have no warehouse assigned.
hint: Test the warehouse reference for the absence of a value.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name, department FROM employees WHERE warehouse_id IS NULL;

title: Newest signups
context: Onboarding reviews the most recent customers.
task: Return first_name, last_name and signup_date with the most recently signed-up customers first.
hint: Sort by signup date, newest at the top.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name, signup_date FROM customers ORDER BY signup_date DESC;

title: Pay review sheet
context: HR is preparing a pay review, grouped by department.
task: Return first_name, department and salary, sorted by department (A to Z) and, within each department, highest paid first.
hint: Two sort keys — the second breaks ties within the first.
answer: SELECT first_name, department, salary FROM employees ORDER BY department, salary DESC;

title: Luxury carousel
context: A carousel showcases the five most expensive products.
task: Return name and price for the five priciest products.
hint: Sort by price, then keep only the top few.
answer: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5;

title: Three biggest orders
context: Leadership wants the largest orders of the period.
task: Return order_id and total_amount for the three largest orders by value.
hint: Largest first, then cut the list short.
answer: SELECT order_id, total_amount FROM orders ORDER BY total_amount DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Inventory value
context: Finance values on-hand inventory at list price.
task: Return name and stock_value (the price multiplied by units in stock, to 2 decimals) for every product.
hint: You'll compute a new column from two existing ones and round it.
answer: SELECT name, ROUND(price * stock, 2) AS stock_value FROM products;

title: Invoice line totals
context: An invoice shows the amount for each line item.
task: Return item_id and line_total (quantity times unit_price) for every order line.
hint: Each line's amount comes from two of its own columns.
answer: SELECT item_id, quantity * unit_price AS line_total FROM order_items;

title: One name column
context: A CRM export needs a single full-name field.
task: Return full_name for every customer, formatted as the first name, a space, then the last name.
hint: Stitch the two name columns together with a space between.
answer: SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name AS full_name FROM customers;

title: Shouty category labels
context: The storefront shows category labels in capitals.
task: Return each product's name and its category in upper case as category_upper.
hint: There's a function that forces text to capitals.
answer: SELECT name, UPPER(category) AS category_upper FROM products;

title: How many Prime members?
context: The quarterly deck needs a single Prime headline number.
task: Return prime_count: how many customers are Prime members.
hint: Count rows, but only the ones that qualify.
answer: SELECT COUNT(*) AS prime_count FROM customers WHERE prime_member = 1;

title: How many customers have ordered?
context: Marketing wants active buyers, not the number of orders.
task: Return active_customers: the number of different customers who have placed at least one order.
hint: The same customer can appear on many orders — count each once.
answer: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_customers FROM orders;

title: Recognised revenue
context: Finance recognises revenue only on delivered orders.
task: Return revenue: the total value of delivered orders, to 2 decimals.
hint: Add up the order totals, but only for delivered ones.
answer: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total_amount), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered';

title: Average order value
context: AOV is a headline metric on the dashboard.
task: Return aov: the average order value across all orders, to 2 decimals.
hint: The mean of the order totals.
answer: SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_amount), 2) AS aov FROM orders;

title: Pay band
context: HR is benchmarking the salary range.
task: Return min_salary and max_salary across all employees in a single row.
hint: The lowest and the highest, side by side.
answer: SELECT MIN(salary) AS min_salary, MAX(salary) AS max_salary FROM employees;

title: Where our customers are
context: A map widget ranks countries by customer base.
task: Return country and customer_count for each country, most populous first.
hint: Collapse to one row per country, then rank by how many.
answer: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY customer_count DESC, country;

title: Order pipeline
context: Ops watches how orders split across the pipeline.
task: Return status and order_count for each status, largest group first.
hint: One row per status; order by the size of each group.
answer: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY order_count DESC, status;

title: Average price by category
context: Pricing compares the typical price across categories.
task: Return category and avg_price (to 2 decimals) for each category.
hint: Average the price within each category.
answer: SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_price FROM products GROUP BY category;

title: Who works where
context: Fulfilment Ops wants each warehouse employee and their site location.
task: Return first_name, last_name and the warehouse location for employees who are assigned to a warehouse.
hint: The location lives on the warehouses table — connect each employee to their warehouse.
answer: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, w.location FROM employees e JOIN warehouses w ON e.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id;
